QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_33

question.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to use a side-pocket arrangement in a Cat III open-ended AIF?

answer.text: An investee has become illiquid due to an idiosyncratic credit event
To protect existing investors from forced liquidation of a distressed asset
To enable new subscribers to enter at a clean NAV excluding the illiquid asset
To delay payment of management fees

explanation.text: The Logic: A side-pocket arrangement segregates an illiquid or stressed asset from the main portfolio so that the main scheme's NAV reflects only liquid holdings — this protects existing investors from forced liquidation, gives new subscribers a clean NAV to enter at, and ring-fences idiosyncratic credit/illiquidity events. It is a portfolio-management and investor-fairness tool, not a fee-deferral tool. Management fees on the side-pocketed portion are typically governed by PPM terms and are not the rationale for creating the side-pocket. The Trap: Options A, B, and C are valid reasons aligned with the side-pocket's purpose of insulating existing investors and providing fair NAV treatment for new and exiting investors. Option D mischaracterises side-pockets as a fee-deferral device, which they are not. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (112, 194, 349, 350) support redemption gates, illiquidity risk, NAV disclosure, and PPM/CTR disclosure, but do not describe side-pocket arrangements or their mechanics. The side-pocket rationale above is general industry/fund-structuring practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
